question: What is the primary purpose of isolation techniques in nursing practice?

options.A: To punish patients with communicable diseases
options.B: To interrupt the transmission of infectious agents to susceptible hosts
options.C: To eliminate the need for hand hygiene
options.D: To reduce the cost of hospital operations

explanation: Isolation techniques are utilized specifically as physical and procedural barriers to interrupt the transmission of infectious agents from an infected source to susceptible individuals. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T15#GNS122_U2_T15_h1)

question: Which of the following is highlighted as a specific high-consequence infectious disease relevant to clinical practice in Nigeria?
explanation: Lassa fever is specifically mentioned alongside Ebola and tuberculosis as high-consequence infectious diseases where isolation protocols are crucial. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T15#GNS122_U2_T15_h1)

question: How do isolation techniques primarily interrupt the chain of infection?

options.A: By targeting the infectious agent's genetic makeup
options.B: By targeting the mode of transmission and portals of entry or exit
options.C: By eliminating the susceptible host entirely
options.D: By increasing the virulence of the pathogen

explanation: Isolation techniques act as physical barriers that primarily disrupt the mode of transmission and block portals of entry or exit. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T15#GNS122_U2_T15_h2)

question: Which of the following represents one of the six links in the chain of infection?
explanation: The portal of exit is one of the classic six links in the chain of infection, alongside the infectious agent, reservoir, mode of transmission, portal of entry, and susceptible host. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T15#GNS122_U2_T15_h2)

question: To which patients should Standard Precautions be applied?

options.C: All patients regardless of their infection status
options.D: Only patients displaying symptoms of fever

explanation: Standard Precautions must be applied universally to the care of all patients, regardless of their diagnosed or presumed infection status. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T15#GNS122_U2_T15_h3)

question: What is the relationship between Standard Precautions and Transmission-Based Precautions?

options.B: Transmission-Based Precautions are used in addition to Standard Precautions.
options.C: Standard Precautions are only used if Transmission-Based Precautions fail.
options.D: They are completely unrelated clinical concepts.

explanation: Transmission-Based Precautions are always implemented in addition to, never in place of, Standard Precautions. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T15#GNS122_U2_T15_h3)

question: Which type of room and respiratory protection is specifically required for Airborne Precautions?

options.A: Positive pressure room and standard cloth mask
options.B: Negative pressure room (AIIR) and fit-tested N95 or higher respirator
options.C: Standard ward bed and face shield only

explanation: Airborne precautions require an Airborne Infection Isolation Room (AIIR) with negative pressure and healthcare workers must wear fit-tested N95 or higher respirators. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T15#GNS122_U2_T15_h4)

question: What protective gear is typically required when entering the room of a patient placed on Contact Precautions?
explanation: Contact Precautions require healthcare workers to wear gowns and gloves upon entering the patient's room to prevent contact transmission. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T15#GNS122_U2_T15_h4)

question: According to standard guidelines, what is typically the first item of PPE to be put on during donning?
explanation: The donning sequence typically begins with putting on the isolation gown first, followed by the mask, eye protection, and gloves. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T15#GNS122_U2_T15_h5)

question: Why is the sequence of doffing PPE critically important?

options.A: To ensure the equipment can be washed and reused for the next patient
options.B: To prevent accidental self-contamination from contaminated outer surfaces
options.C: To speed up the nurse's shift change routine
options.D: To comply with fashion standards in the hospital

explanation: Meticulous doffing sequences are essential to avoid touching contaminated outer surfaces of the PPE, thereby preventing self-contamination. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T15#GNS122_U2_T15_h5)

question: What is the primary definition of engineering controls in infection prevention?

options.A: Physical modifications to the healthcare setting to remove or isolate workplace hazards
options.B: Strict administrative rules regarding nurse break times
options.C: The chemical composition of surface disinfectants
options.D: The personal discipline of individual healthcare workers

explanation: Engineering controls refer to physical changes built into the environment, such as ventilation systems and negative pressure rooms, to isolate or remove hazards. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T15#GNS122_U2_T15_h6)

question: What practice is utilized when single-room isolation is unavailable and patients with the same pathogen are grouped together?
explanation: Cohorting involves grouping patients infected with the same micro-organism together in a shared space when single rooms are unavailable. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T15#GNS122_U2_T15_h6)

question: What is a common psychological effect experienced by patients placed in isolation?
explanation: Physical separation and covered PPE can lead to feelings of loneliness, anxiety, stigmatization, and sensory deprivation for isolated patients. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T15#GNS122_U2_T15_h7)

question: How can a nurse best mitigate the psychosocial impacts of isolation for a patient?

options.A: By minimizing all verbal and non-verbal interactions to save time
options.B: By explaining the clinical rationale and facilitating communication with loved ones
options.C: By removing isolation precautions entirely when the patient feels lonely
options.D: By discouraging any form of entertainment in the room

explanation: Nurses can reduce anxiety by explaining the reasons for isolation, offering reassuring communication, and helping patients connect with family via technology. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T15#GNS122_U2_T15_h7)

question: What attitude should nursing students cultivate regarding near-misses and protocol breaches in clinical practice?

options.A: Hide them to avoid administrative trouble
options.B: Ignore them if no patient was directly harmed
options.C: Encourage a safety culture of open reporting and accountability

explanation: Cultivating a safety culture means encouraging open reporting of near-misses and breaches to improve overall safety and prevent future incidents. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T15#GNS122_U2_T15_h8)

question: Which of the following is highlighted as a vital tool for maintaining high standards of infection control amidst heavy workloads?

options.B: Avoiding the use of clinical checklists
options.C: Reducing hand hygiene frequency to save time
options.D: Delegating all safety protocols entirely to ward attendants

explanation: Peer accountability and self-auditing help nurses maintain high standards of care and prevent slips in technique even in busy environments. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T15#GNS122_U2_T15_h8)
